newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open weak, funds stay sidelined.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open weak, funds stay sidelined.

text.p: Singapore shares opened weaker on Monday with fund managers firmly on the sidelines in the absence of news to lift a lacklustre market, dealers said.
"I think the fund managers have thrown in the towel already and I can't blame them," a dealer at a local brokerage said.
Poor economic numbers, mixed corporate results and jitters over U.S. interest rate rises all conspired to keep the market uncertain, another dealer said.
At 0225 GMT, the barometer Straits Times Industrials Index was off 19.42 points at 2,079.50. Early traded volume was a low 37.7 million shares.
Banks and blue chips led the downward charge, with UOB and DBS foreign share tranches both down Singapore $0.40 at S$14.80 and S$17.10 respectively.
Cycle & Carriage stock also saw an early S$0.40 drop to S$14.50.

Brighter news came from OCBC Bank however. Its stock surged S$0.50 to S$9.60 after it proposed 1-for-5 bonus issue and announced a 17.2 percent profit rise to S$708.9 million on Thursday after the market closed for the Good Friday holiday.
